title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & tools
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical Company Handbook reference for new and existing employees at Redwood Inference. It covers: what it’s like to work here, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding overview, and a high-level guide to the internal tools you’ll use every day. Use the table of contents below to jump to relevant sections.

Table of contents
1. Working at Redwood (culture & expectations)
2. Roles & career ladders (engineers, product, go-to-market, support, people-ops)
3. Benefits & perks (summary + enrollment)
4. Hiring & onboarding overview (process and new hire checklist)
5. Internal tools & guides (access and quick start)
6. FAQs and ownership

---

1) Working at Redwood — Culture, values, and expectations

Intro: Redwood is an engineering-first, product-focused company building inference infrastructure for production ML. We value clarity, ownership, and pragmatic engineering. This section summarizes cultural norms, working patterns, and expectations for contributors at all levels.

Key cultural principles
- Ship with quality: bias to tested, observable changes.
- Ownership and clarity: teams own services, runbooks, and SLOs end-to-end.
- Customer-first engineering: prioritize reliability and predictable cost for customers.
- Continuous improvement: postmortems without blame and measurable follow-ups.

Working patterns and norms
- Async-first communication: document decisions in Confluence and use threads for focused discussions.
- Meetings: keep meetings outcome-oriented and optional; use shared agendas.
- 1:1s: managers should have weekly or biweekly 1:1s; use them for development, blockers, and career conversations.
- On-call: engineering teams have rotating on-call; see the oncall_and_incident_response runbook for escalation steps.

Performance & feedback
- Quarterly reviews: goals set with managers; performance calibration happens across peer groups.
- Career conversations: encouraged at every promotion cycle — see Roles & career ladders section below for competency expectations.

---

2) Roles & career ladders

Purpose: Provide clear expectations for levels, promotion criteria, and how to plan career development at Redwood. The summary below highlights the main families; team-specific ladders are maintained by each group and linked from this page.

Role families covered
- Engineering (eng-serving-runtime, eng-infra, eng-platform, eng-sre, eng-developer-experience)
- Product & design
- Applied ML & Research
- Customer Success & Support
- Sales & Go-to-market
- People Ops, Finance & Legal

Career ladder summary (compact)
- IC1 — New grad / early IC: learns the codebase, delivers defined tasks, asks for reviews.
- IC2 — Experienced individual contributor: delivers features end-to-end, owns small subcomponents, mentors interns.
- Senior / IC3 — Senior IC: leads medium-scope projects, drives design, coaches others.
- Staff / IC4 — Staff engineer or senior product lead: sets technical direction, cross-team influence.
- Principal / IC5+ — Company-wide impact, technical strategy, cross-org leadership.

Promotion signals (what reviewers look for)
1. Consistent delivery of high-quality work that matches scope for level.
2. Demonstrated ownership and ability to drive cross-team projects.
3. Impact metrics: latency/cost improvements, customer adoption, reliability gains, or product KPIs.
4. Mentorship and knowledge sharing: documentation, code reviews, and training.

Example competencies for engineers (summary table)
| Area | IC2 | Senior (IC3) | Staff (IC4) |
|------|-----:|------------:|-----------:|
| Execution | Delivers features with guidance | Owns medium projects end-to-end | Drives large initiatives across teams |
| Design | Contributes to designs | Proposes robust designs for system-level problems | Sets architecture and trade-offs for the org |
| Leadership | Provides peer-level feedback | Mentors and improves team practices | Influences roadmap and cross-team priorities |

Career planning & resources
- Ask your manager for a promotion rubric specific to your team.
- People Ops offers career coaching and a mentorship program; request via the People Ops portal.
- Engineering learning budget: refer to the People Ops training page for eligibility and submission steps.

---

3) Benefits & perks (summary + enrollment)

Employee benefits at a glance (high level)
- Health: medical, dental, and vision plans with family coverage options.
- Financial: 401(k) plan with company match, equity grants per role/level, and commuter benefits where available.
- Time off: flexible PTO policy, 12 company holidays, parental leave policy (birth/adoption), and caregiver leave.
- Wellness: monthly wellness stipend, EAP (employee assistance program), and mental health resources.
- Learning & development: annual training stipend and conference budget for engineers.

Enrollment & timelines
- New hires: benefits enrollment window opens on day 1 and must be completed within 30 days of start date.
- Open enrollment: annual period in November — updates take effect January 1.
- Equity & compensation: stock grants are issued at onboarding and periodically at performance milestones; contact People Ops for vesting schedule details.

How to enroll (step-by-step)
1. Log into the Benefits Portal (HR system) using SSO.
2. Complete your personal information and dependent details.
3. Select plans, review premiums, and submit enrollment.
4. Save confirmation PDFs and share with People Ops if you need manual adjustments.

Benefits table (examples)
| Benefit area | Highlights | Enrollment timing | Owner |
|--------------|-----------|-------------------|-------|
| Medical | Multiple plan tiers + HSA option | New hire window / Open enrollment | People Ops |
| 401(k) | Company match up to 4% | Eligible after 30 days | Finance |
| Parental leave | 16 weeks primary parental leave | Request via People Ops at onboarding | People Ops |

---

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring philosophy
- Candidate experience: fast, transparent, and respectful.
- Role clarity: every job posting includes a public-facing role summary and an internal hiring rubric.
- Bias reduction: structured interviews and standard rubrics for every stage.

High-level hiring process
1. Requisition approval: hiring manager files a req and gets budget approval.
2. Sourcing & screening: recruiters screen and coordinate take-home exercises where applicable.
3. Interview loop: structured interviews (technical, system design, behavioral, culture fit). Hiring panel uses a shared rubric.
4. Offer & negotiation: People Ops and hiring manager approve.
5. Background checks and reference checks.

New hire onboarding timeline (30/60/90)
- Preboarding (before day 1): IT account creation, access to Slack, calendar invites for orientation, and reading list emailed.
- Day 1–7: orientation, meet team, accounts and tool access, benefits sign-up.
- 30 days: deliver first small ticket, check-in with manager on OKRs and goals.
- 60 days: ownership of a primary area and begin a cross-team sync.
- 90 days: performance check / new-hire review; set Q2 objectives.

New hire checklist (must-complete items)
- [ ] Complete HR paperwork and benefits enrollment
- [ ] Confirm workstation setup and VPN access
- [ ] Gain access to core repos (git.redwood.company/*) and internal docs
- [ ] Complete security training and code of conduct course
- [ ] Join relevant Slack channels and cross-team meetings
- [ ] Meet with mentor / onboarding buddy

Onboarding resources and buddies
- Every new hire is assigned an onboarding buddy for the first 8 weeks. Buddies help with context, introductions, and practical workflows.
- Team onboarding docs: each team maintains a "team-setup" Confluence page with runbooks and common issues. Link to the team pages is available from the People Ops onboarding portal.

5) Internal tools & quick-start guides

This section lists the core internal tools, why we use them, and a one-paragraph quick-start for each. For detailed guides see the eng-developer-experience and eng-infra spaces.

Core tools
- Slack (communication): primary realtime comms. Key channels: #all, #eng, #product, #incident, #oncall. Use threads for focused discussions.
- Google Workspace (docs & slides): single source for collaborative docs. Confluence is used for long-lived policies and runbooks.
- Git (git.redwood.company): code hosting and PR workflows. Default branch protections: main protected, require 2 reviewers for services, 1 reviewer for docs.
- CI/CD (build.redwood.company): pipeline templates live in eng-infra; use the "service-template" repo for new services.
- Observability (console.redwood.company): per-route/model dashboards, SLOs and traces. Engineers should set up alerting and SLIs for new services.
- Secrets & key management (vault.redwood.company): store secrets and KMS integrations. Access requests via the security ticketing queue.
- HR & Benefits portal (hr.redwood.company): onboarding forms, payroll, and benefits enrollment.

Quick start examples
- Git & PR: clone git.redwood.company/<team>/<repo>, create a feature branch named feature/<short-desc>, push, and open a PR against main. Link the PR to the relevant Jira ticket.
- Observability: create an SLO for new HTTP endpoints with a latency target and error budget. Add a dashboard tile for p95 latency and set an alert at 2x the SLO.

Access & permissions
- Requests: request tool access via the "Access Requests" workflow in the internal portal. Team leads approve repo and environment access.
- Least privilege: production access requires two approvals and completion of production access training.

Tooling runbook snippets (examples)
- How to request a service account token:
  1. Open the Access Requests form in the internal portal.
  2. Select "service account" and attach the IAM policy you need.
  3. Team lead approves; infra provisions the token and emails the service owner.
- How to onboard a new repo into CI/CD:
  1. Create repo using the service-template.
  2. Add pipeline.yaml and ensure unit tests run in <15m on main.
  3. Add required environment variables in vault and request secrets read access.

6) FAQs, owners, and escalation points

Frequently asked questions
Q: Who do I contact for payroll or benefits questions?
A: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.company) — see the People Ops portal for forms.

Q: How do I request access to production?
A: Submit an Access Requests ticket; your manager must approve and you must pass production access training.

Escalation owners (primary contacts)
- People Ops: Aisha Patel (people-ops@redwood.company)
- IT / Workstation provisioning: it-support@redwood.company
- Security & Incident Response: security@redwood.company (see security-and-compliance pages for runbooks)

Document ownership and updates
- Owner: People Ops (owner_team). People Ops maintains this page and coordinates with Eng, Finance, and Security for updates.
- Review cadence: annual review in Q4 and ad-hoc updates as policy changes.
